summary: Kristin Scheible is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her BA from Colby College and MTS from Harvard. Guided by Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, she became a professor at Reed College.

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. A PhD candidate and editor at Lund University in the 2000s, she was attested as an assistant professor of religious studies at Linnaeus University in 2014.

Sinologist and religious studies scholar Kristofer Schipper studied at the École du Louvre, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held positions at the EFEO (~1962–1973), EPHE (1972–2002), Collège de France, and Fuzhou University (~2004–2021).

Kristóf Szitár works in Iranian, Central Asian, religious, and Indological studies. He studied at Central European University and the University of Lausanne (PhD 2021–2026), and held teaching appointments at Lausanne, Heidelberg (2024), and Yerevan State University (2026).

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA in Tibetan and Mongolian majors (~1997–2009) and served as a research fellow (~2009) at Eötvös Loránd University.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned her PhD from the University of Calcutta, attested in 1966.

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha and earned degrees from Allahabad, Calcutta, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He taught at Allahabad from 1924, becoming professor in 1956, and directed Sampurnanand's Research Institute.

Kshitimohan Sen was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned an MA in Sanskrit from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked for Chamba State's Department of Education (~1904–1908) before joining Visva-Bharati University in 1908, serving as Adhyaksha (1953–1954).

Kumataro Kawada was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, receiving a doctorate in 1941. He served as professor at Japan Women's University (1927), Tokyo University (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).
Kumja Paik Kim is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate at Stanford University and served as curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum beginning in 1989.
Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is an Indologist and historian. She studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay and was attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Kun Chang was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Academia Sinica (~1941–1947), the University of Washington (1951), and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara, earning his degrees at Kyushu University. He held professorial posts at Saga University (~1976–1989) and Saga Medical School (~1986–1993).
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1962 to 1970. He later held an academic post at Meiji Gakuin University from around 1977 to 2014.

Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga (~1967–1976) and served as a professor at Kyoto University from approximately 1992 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1928 to 1931. He subsequently served on the faculty at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied law at the University of Tokyo (~1897–1900). He held governmental and newspaper positions before teaching at Keio University (~1946–1950) and Kokugakuin University (~1949–1962).

Kuno Fischer was a German philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig (~1844–1845) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1845–1847). He served as a professor at the University of Jena (~1856–1872) and Heidelberg University (~1872–1906).

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who completed a PhD at Kiel University and his Habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1883). He held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919).
